The CDE knows three geographies: the nation, a state, and a single agency.
There is no "county" or "city" endpoint. Crime in a county is reported by the
sheriff, by each city police department, by campus police, by transit police,
by the state highway patrol, each under its own agency identifier (ORI).

`fbiCDE` builds county, city and metro-area views by working out which
agencies belong to a geography and querying each of them. That is an
*attribution* model: an agency belongs to a county because the CDE attributes
it there, not because its jurisdiction has been intersected with the county's
boundary. This vignette shows how membership is decided, what the itemised
results look like, and how to add them up without fooling yourself.

Everything below was run against the live API on
2026-10-06.


```r
library(fbiCDE)
```

## Who polices a county

`county_agencies()` lists every agency attributed to a county, from the
bundled agency table, with no network call:


```r
alameda <- county_agencies("Alameda", "CA")
nrow(alameda)
#> [1] 21
table(alameda$agency_class)
#> 
#>         campus county_primary      municipal        special          state 
#>              2              1             14              3              1
```

Each agency gets an `agency_class` from its CDE agency type:

| Class | What it holds | Queried by default? |
|---|---|---|
| `county_primary` | the sheriff (or parish) | yes |
| `municipal` | city and town police | yes |
| `campus` | university and college police | yes |
| `state` | state police, highway patrol, other state agencies | with `include_statewide = TRUE` |
| `special` | transit, school, airport, port, park and railroad police; task forces | only via `agency_class` |
| `tribal` | tribal police | only via `agency_class` |

The default set is the agencies whose jurisdiction is a specific area below
the state. Campus police are in it: their students and staff are part of the
county's population, and leaving their arrests out would understate the
county. State agencies are opt-in because some of their records are statewide
headquarters attributed to whichever county they sit in. Special-purpose
agencies mix single-site forces with multi-county task forces, and how tribal
agencies should map to counties is unresolved, so both are only queried when
asked for by name.


```r
alameda[!alameda$agency_class %in% c("county_primary", "municipal", "campus"),
        c("agency_name", "agency_class")]
#>                                             agency_name agency_class
#> 15              East Bay Regional Parks: Alameda County      special
#> 17               Union Pacific Railroad: Alameda County      special
#> 18 San Francisco Bay Area Rapid Transit: Alameda County      special
#> 21                       Highway Patrol: Alameda County        state
```

## Crime, agency by agency

`get_county_crime_detail()` queries each member agency and returns the results
**unsummed**: one row per agency per month.


```r
detail <- get_county_crime_detail("Alameda", "CA", offense = "V",
                                  from = "01-2020", to = "12-2021")
nrow(detail)
#> [1] 408
head(detail[, c("agency_name", "period", "count", "population",
                "participated_population", "reported")])
#>                       agency_name  period count population
#> 1 Alameda County Sheriff's Office 01-2020    60     130662
#> 2 Alameda County Sheriff's Office 02-2020    62     130662
#> 3 Alameda County Sheriff's Office 03-2020    52     130662
#> 4 Alameda County Sheriff's Office 04-2020    59     130662
#> 5 Alameda County Sheriff's Office 05-2020    65     130662
#> 6 Alameda County Sheriff's Office 06-2020    75     130662
#>   participated_population reported
#> 1                  130662     TRUE
#> 2                  130662     TRUE
#> 3                  130662     TRUE
#> 4                  130662     TRUE
#> 5                  130662     TRUE
#> 6                  130662     TRUE
```

`reported` separates "reported zero" from "did not report". That distinction
is the whole story for California in 2021, when agencies moved to NIBRS and
many stopped reporting for months:


```r
reporting <- stats::aggregate(reported ~ period, data = detail, FUN = sum)
reporting$agencies <- length(unique(detail$ori))
reporting[reporting$period %in% c("06-2020", "12-2020", "01-2021",
                                  "06-2021", "12-2021"), ]
#>     period reported agencies
#> 2  01-2021        0       17
#> 11 06-2020       17       17
#> 12 06-2021        1       17
#> 23 12-2020       17       17
#> 24 12-2021        5       17
```

## Adding it up

`get_county_crime()` sums the detail into one county series, and never hands
back a bare rate: each row carries the denominator it used and the
`coverage_fraction`, the share of the population whose agencies reported that
month.


```r
county <- get_county_crime(detail)
county[county$period %in% c("06-2020", "06-2021"),
       c("period", "count", "population", "rate", "coverage_fraction")]
#>     period count population       rate coverage_fraction
#> 11 06-2020   792    1673000 47.3401076       1.000000000
#> 12 06-2021    11    1663468  0.6612691       0.007255324
```



In June 2020 the reporting agencies covered 100% of Alameda's
population; in June 2021, 1%. The 2021 count is not a crime
drop, and its rate against the full population is not comparable to 2020's.
`denominator = "participated_pop"` divides by the covered population instead,
which keeps the rate meaningful wherever coverage is partial.

## Filling gaps

`impute_reporting_gaps()` fills a month an agency missed *between* months it
reported, by interpolating its rate and scaling by its population. It never
fills before an agency's first report or after its last, and flags every
filled row:


```r
filled <- impute_reporting_gaps(detail)
table(reported = filled$reported, imputed = filled$imputed)
#>         imputed
#> reported FALSE TRUE
#>    FALSE   145   39
#>    TRUE    224    0
```

Imputation is opt-in and visible: the raw detail is never altered, and
`participated_population` stays missing on imputed rows, so coverage still
shows the month as unreported.

## Agencies in more than one county

Some agencies police several counties. Columbus PD covers parts of Delaware,
Fairfield and Franklin counties, and is attributed to each:


```r
franklin <- county_agencies("Franklin", "OH")
franklin[franklin$ori == "OHCOP0000",
         c("agency_name", "county_name", "agency_county_names")]
#>                   agency_name county_name           agency_county_names
#> 35 Columbus Police Department    FRANKLIN DELAWARE; FAIRFIELD; FRANKLIN
```

`county_name` is the county you asked about; `agency_county_names` keeps the
agency's full list. Because such an agency counts in full in each of its
counties, **do not add counties together** to get a larger area: the shared
agencies would be counted more than once. Use a metro area instead.

New York City is the extreme case. The CDE gives three agencies no county at
all, although each polices a whole county or county-equivalent: the NYPD, the
District of Columbia's Metropolitan Police and the Baltimore City Sheriff. The
package attributes them itself (see `?county_agencies`). The NYPD is the police
of all five boroughs and reports one citywide series, so every borough returns
New York City's figures:


```r
queens <- get_county_crime_detail("Queens", "NY", from = "01-2023", to = "03-2023")
queens[, c("agency_name", "period", "count", "population")]
#>                       agency_name  period count population
#> 1 New York City Police Department 01-2023  4431    8184044
#> 2 New York City Police Department 02-2023  3927    8184044
#> 3 New York City Police Department 03-2023  4173    8184044
```

That population is the city's, not Queens'. There is no borough breakdown in
the CDE.

## A city

A city's crime is reported by its own police department, so
`place_agencies()` resolves a place by name:


```r
place_agencies("Lufkin", "TX")[, c("ori", "agency_name", "agency_class", "county_name")]
#>         ori              agency_name  agency_class county_name
#> 1 TX0030400 Lufkin Police Department place_primary    ANGELINA

lufkin <- get_place_crime_detail("Lufkin", "TX", from = "01-2023", to = "06-2023")
lufkin[, c("agency_name", "period", "count", "reported")]
#>                agency_name  period count reported
#> 1 Lufkin Police Department 01-2023    10     TRUE
#> 2 Lufkin Police Department 02-2023    13     TRUE
#> 3 Lufkin Police Department 03-2023    19     TRUE
#> 4 Lufkin Police Department 04-2023    17     TRUE
#> 5 Lufkin Police Department 05-2023    22     TRUE
#> 6 Lufkin Police Department 06-2023    22     TRUE
```

Each city agency also carries the Census code of the unit it polices, for
joining Census data. A city, town or village has a 7-digit `place_fips`; a
township, or a New England or New York town, is a county subdivision rather
than a Census place, and has a 10-digit `cousub_fips` instead:


```r
codes <- c("place_name", "place_type", "place_fips", "cousub_fips")
place_agencies("Lufkin", "TX")[, codes]
#>   place_name   place_type place_fips cousub_fips
#> 1     Lufkin incorporated    4845072        <NA>
place_agencies("Hamilton Township", "NJ", county = "Mercer")[, codes]
#>          place_name         place_type place_fips cousub_fips
#> 1 Hamilton Township county_subdivision       <NA>  3402129310
```

Codes are matched by name among the Census units in the agency's own county,
and follow the 2020 Census vintage. About 99% of city agencies
resolve; regional departments that police several towns get `NA`.

Campus police inside a city cannot be found by name. With the `sf` and `tigris`
packages installed, `add_place_spatial_members()` adds them by locating each
agency's headquarters within the city's boundary; they are then queried along
with the city's own department:


```r
berkeley <- add_place_spatial_members(place_agencies("Berkeley", "CA"))
get_place_crime_detail("Berkeley", "CA", agencies = berkeley,
                       from = "01-2023", to = "12-2023")
```

## Metro areas

A metro area (a Core Based Statistical Area) is a set of whole counties, so
`metro_agencies()` is the union of its counties' agencies, with each agency
counted once:


```r
head(list_metros(type = "metro"))
#>   cbsa_code                  cbsa_title cbsa_type n_counties
#> 1     10180                 Abilene, TX     metro          3
#> 2     10380               Aguadilla, PR     metro          7
#> 3     10420                   Akron, OH     metro          2
#> 4     10500                  Albany, GA     metro          4
#> 5     10540                  Albany, OR     metro          1
#> 6     10580 Albany-Schenectady-Troy, NY     metro          5

columbus <- metro_agencies("Columbus, OH")
nrow(columbus)
#> [1] 96
sum(columbus$ori == "OHCOP0000")
#> [1] 1
```

Large metros mean hundreds of requests, so `get_metro_crime_detail()` refuses
to start above `max_agencies` (150 by default) before sending anything:


```r
get_metro_crime_detail("New York-Newark-Jersey City, NY-NJ",
                       from = "01-2023", to = "12-2023")
#> Error: Metro 'New York-Newark-Jersey City, NY-NJ' resolves to 455 agencies, above max_agencies = 150. Each agency is a separate request, so this would take a while. Raise the limit (max_agencies = Inf), or narrow the set with agency_class.
```

A small area runs quickly:


```r
aberdeen <- get_metro_crime_detail("Aberdeen, WA", from = "01-2023",
                                   to = "03-2023", progress = FALSE)
aberdeen[, c("agency_name", "agency_class", "period", "count", "reported")]
#>                             agency_name   agency_class  period count reported
#> 1  Grays Harbor County Sheriff's Office county_primary 01-2023     4     TRUE
#> 2  Grays Harbor County Sheriff's Office county_primary 02-2023     9     TRUE
#> 3  Grays Harbor County Sheriff's Office county_primary 03-2023     8     TRUE
#> 4            Aberdeen Police Department      municipal 01-2023    10     TRUE
#> 5            Aberdeen Police Department      municipal 02-2023     5     TRUE
#> 6            Aberdeen Police Department      municipal 03-2023     5     TRUE
#> 7                Elma Police Department      municipal 01-2023     0     TRUE
#> 8                Elma Police Department      municipal 02-2023     0     TRUE
#> 9                Elma Police Department      municipal 03-2023     0     TRUE
#> 10            Hoquiam Police Department      municipal 01-2023     3     TRUE
#> 11            Hoquiam Police Department      municipal 02-2023     1     TRUE
#> 12            Hoquiam Police Department      municipal 03-2023     0     TRUE
#> 13           McCleary Police Department      municipal 01-2023    NA    FALSE
#> 14           McCleary Police Department      municipal 02-2023    NA    FALSE
#> 15           McCleary Police Department      municipal 03-2023    NA    FALSE
#> 16          Montesano Police Department      municipal 01-2023     0     TRUE
#> 17          Montesano Police Department      municipal 02-2023     1     TRUE
#> 18          Montesano Police Department      municipal 03-2023     1     TRUE
#> 19         Cosmopolis Police Department      municipal 01-2023    NA    FALSE
#> 20         Cosmopolis Police Department      municipal 02-2023    NA    FALSE

#> 22           Oakville Police Department      municipal 01-2023     1     TRUE
#> 23           Oakville Police Department      municipal 02-2023     0     TRUE

```

## Census populations

The CDE's own populations are usually the right denominator. To use an
external one, `join_census_pop()` adds an American Community Survey county
population (it needs the `censusapi` package and a free Census API key), and
`get_county_crime(denominator = "census_pop")` divides by it:


```r
detail <- get_county_crime_detail("Alameda", "CA",
                                  from = "01-2019", to = "12-2019")
with_pop <- join_census_pop(detail)
get_county_crime(with_pop, denominator = "census_pop")
```
